rock.why: B's fissures actually light their stone and its beam-lit faces keep their form instead of blowing out. Both directly serve the brief. The rest is identical, so the gain is moderate.

lighting.why: B's glowing fissures are a real step toward 04, but it blows out all three cores into flat discs and weakens the beam on the surfaces it hits across five shots, so A meets the 'glow' and 'light lands' rules better overall.

identity.why: B's faceted, world-tinted cores are a clear identity win at the climax of each world, which outweighs its regression: the deep fissures lost their glow halo, and that should be restored from A.

fluids.why: B's fissure glow is a real gain toward reference 04, but its overexposed flat-disc cores break the hero object in all three core shots. The fix is A's cores combined with B's fissures.

characters.why: B improves pilot trim and shellback light spill, but its glimmerfly frame floods the dark with red haze and the stillwalker is cropped out, which costs more than those gains.

vaults.why: B's lit ledge tops and glowing doors make footing noticeably more legible, especially in Return and Kindled. Its pin-shaped fangs are a hazard-readability regression to revert.

ui.why: The UI and HUD are identical in every shot. The only visible differences are in world lighting (B's lamp beam and lit tiles are slightly dimmer in hud-play and veil3-surface), and that falls outside this category.

minerals.why: A and B are pixel-near-identical in every shot; only trivial pose differences appear on the mimic, so they get the same score.
